feature.title: 着手・将棋ルール・詰み・投了

source.needle: pub fn play(&mut self, player: Player, mv: Move) -> Result<MoveOutcome, CommandError> {

flow: MakeMove and Resign validate wire IDs and required expected sequence; move input is parsed as strict USI before entering the application.
The actor derives the side from immutable participant bindings and stages a cloned game; domain rules apply only legal moves, and errors preserve observable state.
The rules adapter generates legal moves including promotion/drop/king safety restrictions; domain logic recognizes checkmate or participant resignation and retains terminal position.
Accepted candidate state enters the atomic receipt/event commit path traced in game-command-recovery; RPC conversion exposes stable acceptance and rejection statuses.

guarantees.statement: Only the bound participants may mutate. The side comes from permanent bindings, moves use strict USI and malformed wire values fail before changing the game.

Legal play supports movement for all ordinary/promoted pieces, blockers, capture/demotion into hand, drops, nifu, dead-rank restrictions, optional/mandatory promotion, king safety/check evasion and pawn-drop-mate rejection.

Checkmate ends the game with the mating side as winner; no moves without check does not cause a loss. Either side may resign off turn, making the opponent winner. Finished games reject new moves/resignations and expose no legal moves.
Domain rejection preserves the whole game, and the application exposes no committed position change from rejected commands. Rules-engine failure remains distinct from ordinary illegality.
Repetition and perpetual-check positions remain playable. There is no clock, timeout, entering-king/declaration or repetition adjudication; pool names do not turn these on.

contracts.statement: Move parsing accepts exactly board USI with optional trailing + or uppercase unpromoted hand-piece drops, with board-bounded squares and no whitespace/extra bytes.

evidence.reason: Square and move invalid forms reject and valid syntax round-trips.
Malformed USI over TCP yields InvalidArgument and unchanged snapshots.

contracts.statement: The adapter generates complete legal moves, looks up the typed request in that set and applies a fallible atomic rules-engine update.

source.needle: pub(crate) fn play(&mut self, mv: Move) -> Result<(), CommandError> {

evidence.reason: Every ordinary/promoted piece movement is compared for both colors.
Sliders stop at friendly pieces and cannot move beyond captured enemies.
Captures demote every promoted kind into hand and a drop consumes a held piece.
Optional nonpromotions remain legal and dead-rank moves require promotion.
Nifu, promoted-pawn exception, occupied-square and unavailable-hand drop cases are asserted.
Pawn/lance/knight dead-rank drops are rejected for both sides.
Pins, legal check evasions and double-check legal moves are asserted.
Pawn-drop mate is rejected while a checking pawn drop with an escape remains legal.
RulesFailure is distinct and preserves state on a rules-engine counter failure.
An ordinary advancing pawn may legally checkmate.
Promotion is allowed when a move starts in the zone and exits it.

contracts.gap: Representative direct fixtures cover each supported rule family, not every reachable position or every rule through a network client.

contracts.statement: Game::play rejects finished or wrong-turn commands, delegates legality, and declares checkmate only when the next side is checked with no legal moves. Repetition/perpetual check are not adjudicated.

evidence.reason: Rejections compare all observable state.
Checkmate returns the terminal winner/reason and later errors prioritize GameFinished.
A side with no legal moves but no check does not automatically lose.
Repeated and perpetual-check positions continue.
A legal TCP sequence asserts accepted capture/promotion/recapture/drop outcomes.

contracts.gap: No clock, timeout, entering-king or declaration adjudicator exists; tests do not enumerate every unsupported adjudication scenario.

contracts.statement: Either participant side may resign while ongoing; result names the opposite side, retains position/turn and rejects later commands.

source.needle: pub fn resign(&mut self, player: Player) -> Result<GameResult, CommandError> {

evidence.reason: Both sides and on/off-turn combinations assert winner and terminal behavior.
TCP resignation checks winner/reason and retained board/hands/turn with empty legal moves.

contracts.statement: The actor checks participant membership before accepted-receipt lookup and derives command side from immutable Participants rather than a caller side choice.

evidence.reason: Outsider move/resign return PermissionDenied, including when reusing a known request ID; seeded distinct participant bindings remain exposed.

contracts.statement: MakeMove validates game/request/user IDs, requires expected_seq, parses USI and forwards a typed application command.

evidence.reason: Malformed IDs, absent sequence and malformed USI are InvalidArgument with no snapshot change.
Generated TCP client accepts capture/promotion/recapture/drop with sequence and result agreement.

contracts.statement: Resign validates game/request/user IDs and required expected sequence, then delegates the authenticated-at-gateway participant claim to the application.

evidence.reason: Malformed resignation fields reject without changes.
TCP resignation returns expected acceptance and terminal result.
Outsider resignation is PermissionDenied.

contracts.statement: Application/domain errors map to stable gRPC classes, including FailedPrecondition for ordinary rejection, PermissionDenied for nonparticipant, Aborted with actual-seq for stale sequence and Internal for rules/infrastructure-internal errors.

evidence.reason: NotFound, wrong-turn/illegal FailedPrecondition, stale Aborted metadata, request correction and post-finish rejection are asserted with unchanged state.
Direct conversion assertions distinguish infrastructure, corruption, rules failure, sequence exhaustion and sequence mismatch status classes.
Checkmate result conversion preserves winner and reason.

limitations: All supported rule families have direct fixture evidence; the selected real-network test covers a representative legal sequence and resignation, not every rule or a full checkmate sequence.
SFEN construction is test-only fixture support, not a public import/editor feature. There is no supported client-controlled game creation RPC.
gRPC caller identities are trusted claims. Browser authentication and spoof rejection are traced in realtime-session-commands-limits.
Links and passing tests do not establish semantic completeness; changes to guarantees, evidence strength and decomposition require review.
